I'm in Edinburgh, Scotland, UK at 2026-09-29 19:59 BST (UTC+0100) (2026-09-29T18:59:00Z in UTC), at latitude 55.9533 degrees and longitude -3.1883 degrees. Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Yes — very likely.

At **5.3° altitude** in the **northeast (azimuth ~60°)**, the Moon is technically above the horizon but quite low: about the width of a fist held at arm’s length above the horizon. With **88% illumination**, it will be bright enough to stand out easily in **nautical twilight**, especially under clear skies.

The main obstacle is not brightness but your local horizon:

- You need a fairly unobstructed view toward the **east-northeast / northeast**.
- Buildings, hills, trees, and haze near the horizon could hide it.
- At only 5° up, atmospheric extinction and low-level cloud/haze can noticeably dim and redden it, but an 88%-lit Moon should still usually be visible if the air is reasonably clear.

Look roughly **NE**, low above the skyline. It may appear somewhat yellow/orange and less crisp than when higher up. If you can see the horizon in that direction, you should have a good chance of spotting it.
